Spring Boot Backend for Frontend

A production-minded gateway for React dashboards.

This portfolio project centralizes JWT security, aggregates user and product APIs, applies Resilience4j fallbacks, and publishes generated API and quality documentation from CI.

Architecture

Request path and resilience boundary

The React client sees one stable dashboard API while the BFF hides downstream contracts and failures.

React Frontend Calls GET /api/dashboard with a Bearer JWT.
down
Spring Boot BFF Validates JWTs, owns the dashboard DTO, and coordinates aggregation.
down
Resilience4j Boundary Wraps WebClient calls with circuit breakers and stable fallbacks.
down
User and Product Services Downstream profile and recommendation APIs stay hidden from the React app.

API Contract

OpenAPI reference for the React-facing contract

CI starts the BFF, exports OpenAPI JSON/YAML, and publishes a static Swagger UI assembled from Springdoc assets.

Developer Experience

Springdoc provides Swagger UI in the local profile for authenticated API exploration with the Authorize button. CI publishes the same contract as a static Swagger UI plus downloadable specs.

Open Swagger UI OpenAPI JSON OpenAPI YAML CI Workflow

Local Swagger UI

Run the BFF with the local profile and open the standard Springdoc route: 

http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html

The spec describes Bearer JWT authentication, stable DTOs, structured errors, and fallback behavior.

Runtime Flow

How a dashboard request is handled

Authenticate

The BFF validates a Bearer JWT before any /api/** request reaches the controller.

Aggregate

The dashboard service reads the JWT subject and starts user and product calls.

Protect

Resilience4j circuit breakers isolate downstream failures and provide fallback responses.

Adapt

The React app receives one stable dashboard response instead of downstream service contracts.

Local Runtime

Run the stack locally

Docker Compose starts the BFF and two WireMock services for realistic local development.

Docker Compose

docker compose up --build

Published ports: BFF on 8080, user service on 8081, product service on 8082.

Authenticated Request

$token = powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\create-local-jwt.ps1
Invoke-WebRequest -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } http://localhost:8080/api/dashboard

Quality Gates

Tests, coverage, and documentation

CI runs one Maven verification path, publishes generated artifacts, and deploys Pages only after success on main.

Behavior Tests

Security, aggregation, downstream HTTP, fallback behavior, DTO JSON, and architecture boundaries.

Coverage Gate

JaCoCo runs during mvn verify and fails the build when configured thresholds are missed.

Generated Docs

OpenAPI specs, Javadoc, and coverage HTML are generated under target and published from CI.
